title: Tirisfal Glades
body: Tirisfal Glades was once the heartland of the kingdom of Lordaeron, a country of misty woods, quiet farms and noble estates in the shadow of the royal capital. When the Plague of Undeath swept through, so many died that mass graves had to be dug, and much of the population rose again as servants of the Scourge. Now the glades belong to the Forsaken, the undead who broke free of the Lich King under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. From the Undercity beneath the ruined capital and from the town of Brill, the Deathguard fight on several fronts at once. Mindless dead still shamble through Deathknell and hold the Agamand Mills, Rot Hide gnolls rob the graves for the Lich King, and more undead slip in past the Bulwark from the Plaguelands. In the northeast the Scarlet Crusade holds its great monastery and sends zealots across the glades to purge every undead they find, free-willed or not.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Tirisfal_Glades (pre-Cataclysm history: part of Lordaeron, mass graves, Forsaken claim the glades, Scarlet Monastery)
quest 363 reward text (freed by Lady Sylvanas)
quest 381 description (Crusade will not rest until every undead, Scourge or no, is destroyed)
notes: verified

title: Deathknell
body: In the hills of western Tirisfal lies Deathknell, where many of the Forsaken first open their eyes to their new existence. The newly risen wake in the crypt above the village, the Shadow Grave, tended by its caretaker Undertaker Mordo, who is ready to toss onto the fire any who fail to stir. Down the road in the chapel, Shadow Priest Sarvis explains to each confused arrival that the Dark Lady has freed them from the Lich King. Executor Arren commands the village, Deathguard Saltain sends recruits to scavenge for usable gear, and Novice Elreth tends the wounded. Mindless zombies and ghouls, their former kin, still wander the northern streets, and a Scarlet Crusade detachment has camped to the southeast.
sources: quest 363 description and reward text (Mordo, caretaker of the crypt; toss you into the fire)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Shadow_Grave (pre-Cataclysm undead characters came to life there)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Deathknell (Arren leads the village; Scarlet camp southeast)

WMOAreaTable.dbc (2117 Shadow Grave is a WMO area)
notes: verified. Shadow Grave (2117) confirmed as a WMO area in WMOAreaTable (root 712), and the undead start point (1676,1678) sits beside Mordo inside it; kept as second trigger.

title: Night Web's Hollow
body: Northwest of Deathknell lies Night Web's Hollow, a small valley around the mouth of an old gold mine. Gold was scarce even when the Alliance stood at the height of its power, and the Forsaken badly need the ore, but spiders have overrun the valley and the tunnels alike. Young spiders prowl the open ground while larger night webs lurk in the shadowed depths of the mine. Executor Arren can spare few hands for the work, so the hollow is being cleared bit by bit. He expects weeks or months to pass before the infestation is gone and the webbing can finally be burned away with torches.
sources: quest 380 description, reward and request texts
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Night_Web's_Hollow (gold mine northwest of Deathknell, young spiders outside, adults within)

title: Solliden Farmstead
body: North of Deathknell, the Solliden Farmstead is a rare sight in Tirisfal: a farm still worked by living humans. Farmer Solliden and his hands tend their pumpkin fields with the Scarlet Crusade close by, its warriors holding a tower to the west beyond the farm, and the farmers side with the Crusaders against all undead. To the Forsaken they are a blight on the land. Deathguard Simmer keeps watch on the road nearby and sends young recruits to steal the farm's pumpkins, which the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill has found a sinister use for.
sources: quest 365 description (farm north of Deathknell, Scarlet Crusade patrols from their tower, steal pumpkins for Apothecary Johaan)
quest 427 description (tower past the Solliden Farmstead)
creature_template: Farmer Solliden 1936, Tirisfal Farmer 1934, Farmhand 1935 use faction 67 (Scarlet Crusade)

notes: verified

title: Cold Hearth Manor
body: Cold Hearth Manor stands beside the main road southwest of Brill, just across a bridge. It was once a farm known for its welcoming hearth and bountiful crops, but the Plague killed everyone who lived and worked there, and its fields have long since gone barren. The Forsaken have taken over the farmhouse, where the tailors Bowen and Constance Brisboise ply their trade for passing travelers. The country around it is far from safe. Rotting dead and ravaged corpses have trickled into the lands west of Brill near the old bridge, and the Deathguard reward those who beat them back.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Cold_Hearth_Manor (warm atmosphere and bountiful crops, Plague killed all, Forsaken took over the farmhouse and trade with travelers)
npc_text 4093 (Bowen's house southwest of Brill just over the bridge at Cold Hearth Manor)
quest 383 description (road passes Cold Hearth Manor)

title: Brill
body: Brill was a human town of the Lordaeron countryside and one of the first to fall to the Plague of Undeath. Today it is the main Forsaken town of the glades, just north of the ruined capital. Magistrate Sevren governs from the town hall, while Executor Zygand directs the Deathguard against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. Apothecaries pursue their experiments, a wanted poster calls for the death of the gnoll Maggot Eye, and the Gallows' End Tavern serves as inn and prison both. North of the town, near the graveyard, stands a sealed mausoleum where the Deathguard hold Ulag the Cleaver, a captured Scourge agent still in thrall to the Lich King.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Brill (human town, one of the earliest afflicted by the Plague; pre-Cataclysm features)
npc_text 4074 (Ruins of Lordaeron to the south)

title: Gallows' End Tavern
body: The Gallows' End Tavern stands on the southeast edge of Brill. Innkeeper Renee offers the weary dead a place to rest their bones, a mage trainer who checked in too late to get a room teaches from the upstairs landing, and Coleman Farthing nurses his bitter grudge against the Agamand family. The cellar has a grimmer purpose. The Deathguard keep prisoners there until they can be properly dealt with, among them a Scarlet zealot and a dwarven mountaineer, and the apothecaries of Brill find such captives convenient subjects for testing their latest brews.
sources: npc_text 4077, 4081, 4085 (tavern on the southeast end of Brill; Cain Firesong on the landing, too late to get a room)
quest 1820 description (Coleman in the Gallows' End Tavern)
quest 492 description (cellar as holding cell until prisoners are properly dealt with)
notes: verified. Area 2119 is a WMO area (WMOAreaTable root 133).

title: Agamand Mills
body: Northwest of Brill, a cluster of windmills marks the Agamand Mills, once the seat of the most prosperous family in Tirisfal. When the Scourge came, the Agamands fortified their home and persuaded their workers to stay and defend it. The defense failed after the younger son Devlin betrayed it to the enemy, and the family and their people perished. Now the Scourge mean to make the mills a base for further attacks on the Forsaken. Skeletal soldiers and darkeye bonecasters crowd the fields, lost souls drift among the windmills, and the dead Agamands themselves walk the grounds as minions of the Lich King.
sources: posarea: Gregor 1654, Devlin 1657, Dargol 1658 in area 157; DB spawns Rattlecage Soldier, Cracked Skull Soldier, Darkeye Bonecaster, Lost Soul there
notes: verified

title: Agamand Family Crypt
body: At the north end of the Agamand Mills stands the family crypt, where generations of Agamands were laid to rest. It is now the strongest Scourge position in the area and the headquarters of Captain Dargol, a skeletal commander who uses necromancy to raise the Agamand ancestors from their tombs. Wailing and rotting dead fill the grounds, ready to be turned against the Forsaken. The crypt also guards the family's heirloom weapons, a sword, an axe, a dagger and a mace, which Coleman Farthing would dearly like to see stripped from the cursed Agamand lands.
sources: DB: Wailing Ancestor 1534 and Rotting Ancestor 1530 spawns around 52,28; Captain Dargol 1658 at 52.8,26.3
notes: verified. Area 158 is a WMO area (WMOAreaTable root 241), so it triggers inside the crypt, not on the open grounds.

title: Garren's Haunt
body: North of Brill, Garren's Haunt was once a prosperous farmstead of farmhouse, barn and wide fields. The Scourge murdered Garren and his family when Lordaeron fell, and the gray, lifeless farm is now the den of the Rot Hide gnolls, corpse thieves in the service of the Scourge who attack anyone who strays too close. The foulest of them is Maggot Eye. To the southwest lie the mass graves dug for the countless dead of the Plague, and the gnolls dig there for bodies to carry off and swell the Lich King's armies.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Garren's_Haunt (pre-Cataclysm section: prosperous farm, Garren and family murdered, Rot Hides and Maggot Eye)
quest 358 description (mass graves southwest of Garren's Haunt)
notes: verified

title: Gunther's Retreat
body: On an island in Brightwater Lake, northeast of Brill, a lone lich has made his home at Gunther's Retreat. Gunther Arcanus broke free of the Lich King's will on his own and, believing himself the only undead ever to do so, set his minions on anyone who approached, Forsaken included. Hungering dead and shambling horrors still guard the island. Off its southern shore stands an old, bloody table used as an altar by Lillith Nefara, a powerful agent of the Scourge, who wakes in wrath when a Candle of Beckoning is lit upon it.
sources: quest 357 description (lich on the island in Brightwater Lake; believes all other undead are Scourge slaves)
gameobject 1557 Lillith's Dinner Table, 1586 Crate of Candles
posarea: Gunther 1497 and Hungering Dead 1527 in area 163, Lillith's table in area 162
notes: Direction corrected: the island (Gunther at 2574,-48) lies northeast of Brill, not east.

title: Balnir Farmstead
body: The Balnir Farmstead lies in eastern Tirisfal on the way to the Plaguelands. Its family once bred the white horses ridden by Lordaeron's royal household, and here Prince Arthas buried his beloved steed Invincible. A plaque still marks the grave, but it lies open, for Arthas returned as a death knight and raised the horse to carry him in undeath. Today the ruined farm is a haven for Scourge that slip past the Bulwark, bleeding horrors and wandering spirits among them, and the Deathguard patrol it closely. Mages of the Undercity gather the snapdragons in its garden to learn whether the taint of the Plaguelands has crept into Tirisfal.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Balnir_Farmstead (royal horse breeders; Invincible born and buried there; Scourge haven)

quests 356, 359 reward text, 1882 description and request text

notes: verified. Invincible's birth, burial and raising come from Arthas: Rise of the Lich King (2009) via the wiki; the grave and plaque are in the 3.3.5 DB (added 3.0.2).

title: Crusader Outpost
body: Crusader Outpost is a ruined tower in eastern Tirisfal near the Balnir Farmstead, held by the Scarlet Crusade to watch the main road through the glades. Its garrison of Scarlet friars answers to Captain Vachon, one of the three captains of the Crusade's Tirisfal Regional Command, and raids out from the tower against the undead. Orders taken from a Scarlet messenger show his superiors warning Vachon of growing undead movement near a northern tower and expecting him to crush it swiftly. Executor Zygand believes the captain's death would badly slow the Crusade's advance across the glades.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Crusader_Outpost (scout tower watching the main road, commanded by Captain Vachon)
posarea: Captain Vachon 1664 in area 167; Scarlet Friar spawns nearby
notes: verified

title: Venomweb Vale
body: Venomweb Vale is a wide valley in eastern Tirisfal, just south of the Scarlet Monastery. It was once a fine hunting ground for deer and rabbits, but it now crawls with vicious night web spiders and takes its new name from them. Their venom is prized by the apothecaries of Brill, who believe it preserves the deadly agent of an ancient plague. The spiders gather around a monstrous one called Sri'skulk. Old tales say the vale was once a meeting place of the Council of Tirisfal, and that one of its members bred the spiders to guard it.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Venomweb_Vale (former hunting ground, spiders led by Sri'skulk, Council of Tirisfal meeting place per the novels)
posarea: Vicious Night Web Spider 1555 and Sri'skulk 10359 in area 812
notes: verified. Council of Tirisfal meeting place and the spiders bred by a Council member come from the wiki (Venomweb Vale, Ethylar), sourced to Warcraft: Legends vol. 5 (2009); pre-3.3.5 and framed as old tales.

title: Whispering Gardens
body: The Whispering Gardens spread across the hill below the entrance of the Scarlet Monastery, the great seat of the Scarlet Crusade in northeastern Tirisfal. Long ago a fierce battle was fought here between a Scourge host and the forces that would become the Crusade, and it is said the spirits of the fallen still murmur in the twilight. Today the gardens, and the hedged Terrace of Repose on the far side of the monastery doors, are thick with Scarlet scouts, magicians and preservers, who guard the approach to the monastery against undead and outsiders alike.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Whispering_Gardens (hill south of the monastery entrance; battle with the Scourge; faint whispers in the twilight; Terrace of Repose adjacent)
npc_text 7206 (Scarlet Monastery in the hills northeast of Tirisfal)

title: Scarlet Watch Post
body: North of the Scarlet Monastery, the Scarlet Watch Post is a scout tower guarding the monastery's less defensible northern side. It stands past Faol's Rest, where the revered Archbishop Alonsus Faol was laid to rest some time before the Plague. The tower's crew of neophytes and vanguards is led by Captain Melrache, a ruthless commander who keeps two bodyguards at his side and raids across northern Tirisfal. His superiors worry over how organized the undead near the Plaguelands border have become, and have promised him fresh men.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Scarlet_Watch_Post (scout tower north of the monastery, commanded by Captain Melrache)
quest 372 description (ruined tower in northern Tirisfal, past Faol's Rest, ruthless commander, two bodyguards)

title: Ruins of Lordaeron
body: South of Brill rise the Ruins of Lordaeron, all that remains of the capital where King Terenas Menethil ruled. In its throne room the king was slain by his own son, Prince Arthas, and the Scourge laid the city waste. A grave in the ruins honors Terenas as the last true king of Lordaeron, praying that the father lie blameless for the deeds of the son. Beneath lies the Undercity, capital of the Forsaken, reached by lifts at the back of the ruins, and zeppelin towers outside the walls link it with distant lands. Not long ago Thrall and Sylvanas gathered the Horde in these ruins before storming the city below to take it back from the traitor Varimathras.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Ruins_of_Lordaeron (throne room where Arthas killed Terenas; Undercity beneath; Battle for the Undercity in Wrath)
page_text 1731 and gameobject 175659 Here Lies King Terenas Menethil II, area 153

DB: Thrall 32518, Sylvanas 32365, Vol'jin 31649 at the ruins entrance (Battle for the Undercity)

title: The Bulwark
body: The Bulwark guards the eastern edge of Tirisfal where the road enters the Western Plaguelands, the Forsaken's last line of defense against the Scourge beyond. High Executor Derrington commands this front, where politics give way to a daily fight for survival and the defenders press toward Andorhal. Members of the Argent Dawn, an order that calls both Horde and Alliance its friends in the war on evil, stand alongside the Forsaken, and apothecaries prepare agents to turn the Scourge's plague cauldrons against their makers. Even so, some undead still slip past into the glades.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/The_Bulwark (Forsaken's last bastion of defense; Forsaken and Argent Dawn defenders)
notes: verified

title: Executor Zygand
body: Executor Zygand commands the Deathguard in Brill, with officers such as Executor Arren at Deathknell and Deathguard Linnea at the eastern waystation reporting to him. With the Lich King's army growing each night the Deathguard have larger worries, so Zygand looks to recruits with initiative to drive the Scarlet Crusade to the grave. When documents seized from a Scarlet messenger revealed the names and positions of the Crusade's officers in Tirisfal, he saw a chance to shatter the zealots' morale by cutting down their leaders in swift succession. He prizes ruthlessness in those who serve the Dark Lady under him.
sources: quest 383 description and reward text (Arren's superior; kill their leaders)
quest 427 description (Lich King's army grows each night; initiative)
quests 370, 371, 372 descriptions and reward texts (ruthless fighters)
notes: 'Particular target' claim corrected per quest 427 (the Deathguard have larger concerns, so he wants recruits with initiative).

title: Magistrate Sevren
body: Magistrate Sevren governs Brill from its town hall, a brisk official who keeps the town's records of the dead and directs its struggle against the Scourge. He relies on fresh reports from the Deathguard waystation near the Plaguelands border, sends agents to stop the Rot Hide gnolls robbing the mass graves, and has marked the Scourge stronghold in the Agamand Family Crypt for destruction. When Bethor Iceshard of the Undercity asked for an agent of proven worth against the Scourge for a dangerous errand, it was Sevren who chose one and sent them south with his orders.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Magistrate_Sevren (Brill Town Hall, known for being brisk)
notes: 'Regular reports' softened to fresh reports (quest 359); 'sealed' orders removed (quest 405 says only orders).

title: Shadow Priest Sarvis
body: Shadow Priest Sarvis waits in the chapel at the foot of the hill in Deathknell, and for many newly risen Forsaken he is the first to explain what has become of them. He tells each one that Lady Sylvanas has freed them from the Lich King, and that the Forsaken now wage war on the Scourge and on the holdouts of humanity alike. No other race on Azeroth, he says, has suffered as their people have, and laughing in the face of death is now second nature to them. He sends every recruit against the mindless dead of the village, regretting only that such numbers cannot be brought into the fold.
notes: verified

title: Gunther Arcanus
body: In life Gunther Arcanus studied among the Kirin Tor of Dalaran with his friends Bethor Iceshard and Thule Ravenclaw, and he became a skilled necromancer. He fell to the Plague, but in time broke free of the Lich King's hold. Believing he was the only undead ever to do so, he withdrew to an island in Brightwater Lake and set his minions on all who came near. When an agent of the Forsaken returned his stolen spellbook bearing Bethor's enchantment, Gunther learned he was not alone. Once the agent had destroyed the Scourge servant Lillith Nefara as proof, he sent a Nether Gem to Bethor so the two old friends could speak again.
sources: quest 366 description (Kirin Tor students; both fell to the Plague)
quest 357 description and reward text (skilled necromancer in life)
notes: 'By his own will' softened; quest 357/409 support only that he is free-willed and thought himself alone.

title: Coleman and Yvette Farthing
body: Coleman Farthing worked the Agamand Mills before the Plague. When the Scourge came, the Agamands fortified their home and talked their workers into staying to defend it, and Coleman, a loyal fool by his own account, died for their pride. Now a Forsaken at the Gallows' End Tavern, he blames the family for his undeath and collects their bones for his mantle, hoping they knew fear at the end. His daughter Yvette had begged Thurman Agamand, the eldest son and her beloved, to flee with them. As a Forsaken she has put love aside as part of a life now over, though she still wondered what became of him.
sources: quest 362 reward text (bones on my mantle)
notes: verified. Daughter relation: wiki infobox cites quest 361, where Yvette begged Thurman to leave the mills with her and her father; shared surname and Coleman's 'me and my family' (quest 362) agree.

title: Devlin Agamand
body: Devlin was the younger of the two Agamand sons, weak and sharp-tongued where his brother Thurman was tall and gentle, and a mystery to his family since childhood. When the Scourge surrounded the mills he despaired and made a pact with them, murdering two watchmen and letting the undead through a breach, and a third of the defenders were slain. Whatever he was promised, he rose like the rest of his family as a servant of the Lich King. He now haunts the road to the mills, cackling that he is head of the family at last and asking his cold master when the promise will be kept.
notes: Faction changed 2 to 0: Devlin (faction 21) is hostile to all and killable by Alliance; matches the original note.

title: Apothecary Johaan
body: Apothecary Johaan of the Royal Apothecary Society works in Brill on a challenge set by Lady Sylvanas herself: to brew a new plague deadlier than any ailment on Azeroth, one that will bring Arthas's Scourge to ruin. He proceeds by trial and error, testing darkhound blood, murloc scales and the venom of night web spiders, and lacing ordinary pumpkins with his formulas. His test subjects come from among the prisoners in the cellar of the Gallows' End Tavern. Mindful of his duty to the Society, he shares his findings with his colleagues at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest.
notes: Faction changed 0 to 2: Johaan uses template 68 (hostile to Alliance) and quest 367 is Horde only.

title: Maggot Eye
body: Maggot Eye is a gnoll of the Rot Hide pack, foul even by gnoll standards, who pillages the lands around Garren's Haunt north of Brill. He has been stealing corpses for the Lich King's armies, and the town of Brill has sentenced him to death for his crimes against the Forsaken. A wanted poster in town promises a reward to whoever carries out the sentence and brings his paw to Executor Zygand, and closes with a blunt reminder that mercy is for the weak.
notes: verified

title: High Executor Derrington
body: High Executor Derrington commands the Forsaken at the Bulwark on Tirisfal's eastern border. He has no patience for the schemes of politicians, for at the Bulwark survival is fought for every day, and he welcomes anyone eager to prove themselves a hero. His eyes are fixed on Andorhal and the lich Araj the Summoner who holds it. He plans to set the Scarlet Crusade and the Scourge at each other's throats with a burned command tent and a planted Scourge banner, and his second, Shadow Priestess Vandis, oversees a scheme to turn the Scourge's own plague cauldrons against them.
sources: quest 5228 description (My second, Shadow Priestess Vandis)
notes: verified

title: Rude Awakening
body: Each new Forsaken in Deathknell begins in the cold of the crypt, greeted by Undertaker Mordo and sent down to Shadow Priest Sarvis, who explains that the Lich King's hold is broken and that the Dark Lady leads the war against the Scourge. The first lesson is to destroy the mindless zombies, ghouls and rattling skeletons in the north of the village, former brothers and sisters who remain the Lich King's slaves. Recruits scavenge the village for gear, and hunt wolves and bats so Novice Elreth can find them armor. Among these first tasks is a gentler one. Marla Fipps was spared undeath only to die at the hands of her husband Samuel, who rose as one of the mindless. Her last wish was to be buried beside him, so his remains are laid in her grave in the first row of the village graveyard.
notes: verified

title: At War with the Scarlet Crusade
body: The Scarlet Crusade hunts every undead in Tirisfal, Scourge or Forsaken, and the Deathguard answer in kind. It begins at Deathknell, where Executor Arren strikes at a Crusade camp to the southeast and has its messenger, Meven Korgal, slain. The documents he carried lay out the Crusade's Tirisfal Regional Command and its orders from the Highlord. In Brill, Executor Zygand turns them into a campaign against the Crusade's leaders. Scarlet warriors fall at the tower beyond the Solliden Farmstead. Then the captains die one by one: Perrine at the ruined tower southwest of Brill, Vachon with his friars near the Balnir Farmstead, and finally Melrache and his two bodyguards in the far north past Faol's Rest. Meanwhile Deathguard Burgess gathers Scarlet insignia rings in the name of Varimathras, then lieutenant to the Dark Lady.
sources: page_text 223, 224 (Tirisfal Regional Command, by order of the Highlord)
notes: Varimathras qualified as 'then' lieutenant, since by 3.3.5 he has turned traitor (Battle for the Undercity).

title: The Fall of House Agamand
body: The Agamands were the wealthiest family in Tirisfal, and their pride became their ruin. When the Scourge came, Gregor Agamand would not abandon his mills. His younger son Devlin despaired and made a pact with the enemy, murdering two watchmen and leading the Scourge through a breach. A third of the defenders died that night, and the rest soon followed. The elder son, Thurman, wrote a last letter to his beloved Yvette Farthing, but it never reached her. Now the dead Agamands serve the Scourge, who mean to make the mills a base against the Forsaken. Coleman Farthing, once their worker, wants the remains of Gregor, Nissa, Thurman and Devlin brought to him. The Deathguard clear the fields, and Magistrate Sevren orders an assault on the family crypt, where Captain Dargol raises the Agamand ancestors to fight.
notes: verified

title: A New Plague
body: Lady Sylvanas has challenged the Royal Apothecary Society to create a new plague, one deadly enough to bring ruin to the Scourge. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan pursues the task step by step. He tests the blood of darkhounds, then the scales of murlocs, and then, after finding an old text about an ancient plague preserved in spider venom, the poison of the vicious night web spiders of eastern Tirisfal. Pumpkins stolen from the Solliden Farmstead and laced with his formula are fed to a starving Scarlet zealot held in the cellar of the Gallows' End Tavern, who soon feels his flesh begin to rot. A captured dwarven mountaineer is served a special drink holding a hint of what the Dark Lady has planned for the rest of Azeroth. Johaan's findings then travel on to his colleagues in Silverpine Forest.
notes: verified

title: The Prodigal Lich
body: Bethor Iceshard, a powerful mage of the Undercity, asked Magistrate Sevren for an agent of proven worth. His quarry was a lich living on an island in Brightwater Lake, free of the Lich King yet convinced that every other undead was still a Scourge slave. To learn who he was, the agent stole his spellbook, and Bethor knew it at once. It belonged to Gunther Arcanus, his friend from their student days among the Kirin Tor, before the Plague claimed them both and their fellow student Thule Ravenclaw went over to the Scourge. Bethor enchanted the book to reveal his own freedom and had it returned. Gunther demanded proof, so the agent lit a Candle of Beckoning on a bloody altar off the island and slew Lillith Nefara when she rose. Convinced, Gunther sent a Nether Gem to Bethor, and the Forsaken won a powerful ally.
notes: verified

title: The Graverobbers
body: When the Plague first came to Tirisfal, the dead were so many that mass graves were dug southwest of Garren's Haunt. Those bodies had been spared undeath until the Scourge sent the Rot Hide gnolls to dig them up and carry them off to swell the Lich King's armies. Magistrate Sevren will not allow it. The Rot Hides are hunted at the graves and at Garren's Haunt, and the embalming ichor that animates them is sent to the apothecaries for study. In time the Forsaken learn that the Rot Hides answer to Thule Ravenclaw, a mage of Dalaran turned Scourge. Brill has also sentenced Maggot Eye, the foulest of the corpse thieves, to death. Nearby, a junior apothecary sends an abomination named Gordo to gather weeds by the graves, and fumes when it keeps bringing back the wrong ones.
